It really depends on your threat model. If you need it to be secure from any particular national government's agency (e.g. the IRS), you have to encrypt before it leaves your computer (and have all your contacts encrypt before sending to you). You can't trust any email provider, and you never will be able to trust one, for that purpose.

Lavabit is who you are remembering. Snowden made them famous.

Email is like a postcard. Anyone with the ability to read and access it can read it. Best practices are to verify the identity of those with which you wish to communicate with signed public keys. Encrypt any message before sending. Insist that anyone that sends you messages does the same. Encrypt and decrypt offline.
